description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop a testbed that will test the interoperability between different suppliers of optical communication terminals. Thisshall include free-space optics testing to evaluate the pointing, acquisition, and tracking performance.TargetedImprovements:To enable independent on-ground validation of optical communication terminal interoperability ina facility located in ESA member states.Description: With an increasing number of constellations considering the use of optical inter satellite links and cross-atmospheric links, it is important to test, validateand ultimately certify the interoperability between different laser terminals manufactured by multiple suppliers.This activity will develop the capability of enabling independent interoperability validation between various laser communication terminals. The focus willbe on pointing, acquisition and tracking performance validation for both intersatellite and cross-atmospheric optical links. title: VERIFICATION OF ADVANCED NAVIGATION ANTENNA - EXPRO+
description: Advanced satellite navigation antennas increasingly incorporate anti-jamming, anti-spoofing and adaptive beamforming capabilities to meet the growing demands of Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) applications. The verification of such antennas requires realistic Over-The-Air (OTA) test environments capable of reproducing complex signal scenarios with multiple simultaneous sources arriving from different directions. Existing test approaches are often limited in their ability to reproduce realistic operational environments, leading to lengthy test campaigns and reduced capability to assess the full radiated performance of advanced navigation antennas.State-of-the-art OTA test systems based on multiple transmitting elements have demonstrated the capability to emulate representative signal environments for navigation applications. Such systems enable controlled reproduction of satellite constellations, interference sources, multipath conditions and other operational scenarios in a laboratory environment. However, current solutions oftensuffer from limited flexibility, restricted angular coverage, significant infrastructure requirements or insufficient scalability to support future generations of advanced navigation antennas.A compact, scalable and flexible OTA radiated test system based on an arrangement of transmitting elements surrounding the Antenna Under Test (AUT) needs to be developed. The developed system shall provide the capability to emulate realistic navigation signal environments, enabling repeatable laboratory verification of advanced navigation antennas and associated signal processing techniques. The system is intended to support the development and validation of future PNT technologies and shall constitute a versatile test capability for advanced navigation antenna assessment.Equipment already available at ESTEC, such as a general waveform generator (e.g. PSG) and signal analyser (e.g. PXA), and necessary for this activity will be reused for test execution.The objectives of this activity are: Develop a scalable OTA architecture based on multiple transmitting elements arranged around the Antenna Under Test. Demonstrate the capability of the system to reproduce multiple simultaneous signal sources with controlled angular distribution. Validate the performance of the developed system through representative OTA test campaigns.

title: QUANTUM COMPUTING ALGORITHMS DEVELOPMENT FOR SPACE APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop and assess quantum computing algorithms, methods and related tools for solving specific spacerelated computational challenges with higher performance and reliability than the state of the art achieved with the classical technologies.Description:Quantum computing technologies are progressing rapidly, with early-stage commercial and academicplatforms offering capabilities relevant to space applications. As one of the strategic sectors expected to benefit from quantum advantage, the space domain offers complex, high-impact challenges that can guide algorithm development and platform requirements. Lessons learned from these applications will be transferable to other sectors, enabling a broader quantum technology ecosystem. This activity aims to ensure European industry is quantum-ready and positioned to lead in the global race for space-enabled quantum technologies. It supports European strategic autonomy by fostering sovereign capabilities in quantum algorithm development, hybrid integration, and secure processing architectures tailored to ESA or national mission needs. The initiative also strengthens Europe's industrial competitiveness by enabling use-case-driven innovation and demonstrating technical leadership in both terrestrial and space environments. This activity aimsto encourage the usage of quantum computing potentials to address the challenges in space missions and technologies. It is expectedto extensively use the precision and fast calculations to solve in the most innovative ways challenges related to, mission planningbooks, AI integration, cryptography, and onboard processing, optimisation algorithm for power batteries, among others. Technology focus areas can include but are not limited to quantum-enhanced simulation for propulsion, materials, thermal, power, satellite station keeping, radiation and orbital dynamics, optimization of tools for mission planning, routing, scheduling, debris avoidance and predictive maintenance, quantum Machine Learning (QML) for Earth Observation, anomaly detection, and FDIR, design of quantumnativepre-measurement processing flows, leveraging intrinsic quantum dynamics to condition mission-criticaldata within the quantum domainpriorto readout or classical interface, digital twin powered by quantumcomputing.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Development and benchmarking of quantum algorithms tailored to space-relevant challengesconsidering gate-based, annealing or hybridquantum computing methods- Ground-based demonstrators for performance validation on quantum computers and/or classical high performance computers- Development of a software tool or product enabling the exploitation of the quantum algorithm for oneor more specific space related use cases- Analysis of the expected performance scaling with future generations of quantum computersThe tasks shall include clearly defined use cases and assess how quantum approachesincluding hybridmethods and error mitigation techniquesperformunder realistic computational loads and spaceenvironments, compared to classical baselines.Deliverables: Software, Report
